deepthink._model_operand_incident_note: 2026-07-31 INCIDENT: this profile silently ran gemini-3.6-flash-high (agy's CCPA fallback) instead of Pro for an unknown prior duration. The 2026-07-27 'live-validated' claim below only confirmed the CLI invocation exited cleanly, not which model actually served the request -- agy's own log (~/.gemini/antigravity-cli or _sys/antigravity/config/log/cli-*.log, lines from model_resolver.go/model_config_manager.go) never surfaces the substitution to stdout. Root cause: agy's --model flag requires the exact human-readable display label agy's own `models` subcommand does NOT print (e.g. "Gemini 3.1 Pro (High)"), not the lowercase-hyphenated catalog slug ("gemini-3.1-pro-high") that `models` enumerates -- the two forms are not interchangeable for this entry. Confirmed by matching the interactive /model picker's own working session against its cli.log line (`Resolving model Gemini 3.1 Pro (High)` -> `Propagating selected model override to backend: label="Gemini 3.1 Pro (High)"`, no CCPA fallback). ag.standard/ag.effort/ag.gptoss/ag.opus were audited the same way same day and are NOT affected -- their bare-slug-plus---effort or single-literal operands resolve correctly; this bug is specific to this one catalog entry's local-config registration in the installed agy build. Re-verify after any agy.exe update by grepping the freshest cli-*.log for 'not in local config' / 'Propagating selected model override' immediately after a live ag.deepthink dispatch -- do not trust a clean exit code alone. 2026-08-01 RE-VERIFICATION (multi-angle currency review): (a) catalog check -- `agy.exe models` still lists no Gemini Pro variant beyond gemini-3.1-pro-high/-low (only 3.6/3.5-flash tiers exist above it), so this remains the best available Gemini Pro option, no remapping needed; (b) live resolution re-checked across 3 independent fresh dispatches today, all showing the correct `Propagating selected model override to backend: label="Gemini 3.1 Pro (High)"` signature -- refined finding: a `Model ID ... not in local config, defaulting to CCPA` line at bare process startup (pid 1, before auth/entitlement completes) is normal transient noise seen on EVERY profile's fresh server spawn (confirmed identically on ag.effort's gemini-3.6-flash log the same day) and is not itself proof of a fallback -- only a `Propagating...` line carrying the wrong label would be; (c) found and fixed a real doc-drift bug: `_sys/docs-v2/specific/ag.md`'s profile table still showed the pre-fix slug+separate-effort format, never updated in the 2026-07-31 fix commit -- corrected. 2026-08-02 CORRECTION: the 'ag.standard/ag.effort/ag.gptoss/ag.opus... are NOT affected' claim above was wrong for standard/effort/gptoss -- it was written from a clean-exit-code assumption, not the log-inspection standard this same note insists on for deepthink, and 84fcb53 (2026-07-27, same day range) had already regressed all three to a bare, non-catalog slug by the time this note was written. Caught by cx.effort's merge-readiness review; all three restored to their correct tier-suffixed catalog slugs (see each profile's own _model_id_regression_note). ag.opus (claude-opus-4-6-thinking) was independently re-confirmed still correct.

gptoss._context_window_note: runtime_context_window=8000 is a CONFIRMED LOWER BOUND, not the model's ceiling: an ag-run sentinel probe (~8k-token prompt with 3 unique markers at start/middle/end, piped via stdin to avoid the Windows CreateProcess 32K arg-length limit) succeeded cleanly and correctly recovered all 3 markers, proving real processing of the full input - NOT just declared/self-reported. An earlier attempt where ag asked the model to self-report its own context window returned an untrustworthy 2048 (cx independently flagged this as a likely hallucination: gpt-oss-120b's public model card documents 128K native context, and '(Medium)' is a reasoning-EFFORT tier, not a context-window tier - it should not shrink the window to 2048). Do not treat 8000 as the true ceiling, and do not write 131072 here unless separately re-validated against THIS hosted deployment (Antigravity), not just the base model's public spec - a higher real bound has simply not been empirically probed yet.

deepthink._context_window_note: 2026-09-08: 14000 is a CONFIRMED LOWER BOUND, not the model's ceiling -- an 8016-word (14,135-token, per codex's own reported usage) sentinel probe with 3 unique markers at start/middle/end succeeded cleanly, correctly recovering all 3 (MARKER_START/MIDDLE/END), proving real processing of the full input, not just declared/self-reported. The prior model's live-confirmed 272000 does not carry over to a different model, and model-registry.json has no gpt-6 entry yet (vendor docs not yet published as of this bump) -- discovered live that hub.py's dispatch-target composition hard-requires a positive runtime_context_window (UnknownModelCapacityError otherwise, blocking every dispatch), so an honest measured-lower-bound value was required here, not an absent/null placeholder. Do not treat 14000 as the true ceiling -- a larger probe has simply not been run yet; re-probe with a bigger sentinel before relying on this number being tight.
deepthink._bump_note: 2026-09-08: bumped from gpt-5.6-sol to gpt-6-astra (new generation, discovered via a fresh Engram/peerhub-side install investigation, no tier suffix exists -- codex has no model-listing command like agy's, so `gpt-6-mini/nano/luna/terra/sol/nova/stella/orion` were all probed and confirmed NOT to exist via a real 400 invalid_request_error before settling on the one bare working name). Bake-off vs gpt-5.6-sol: 1 clean deterministic task (4-step conditional-swap arithmetic puzzle) -- both models answered correctly, gpt-5.6-sol slightly faster (7.5s vs 9.6s); a second code-reasoning task was inconclusive due to a shell-quoting harness bug on both sides (not a model difference). This is a real but narrow, non-discriminating probe per this doc's own established 'easy probes don't discriminate frontier reasoning' finding -- not strong evidence of a capability gain, just confirmation the new model works and isn't worse. cx.standard/cx.effort deliberately left on the proven gpt-5.6 family (luna/terra) pending their own evidence.
